0: ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR THE LICENSURE AND SALE OF PACKAGED DISTILLED SPIRITS WITHIN THE JURISDICTION OF THE TOWN OF BETWEEN GEORGIA
1:
AN ORDINANCE TO ALLOW FOR THE PACKAGE SALE OF DISTILLED SPIRITS AND TO PROVIDE FOR THE LICENSURE, CONTROL, TAXATION, AND REGULATION FOR THE PACKAGE SALE OF DISTILLED SPIRITS WITHIN THE JURISDICTION OF THE TOWN OF BETWEEN, GEORGIA; TO AUTHORIZE A REFERENDUM; TO PROVIDE FOR ADOPTION AND AN EFFECTIVE DATE; AND FOR OTHER LAWFUL PURPOSES.

WHEREAS, the Mayor and Town Council of the Town of Between, Georgia (hereinafter “Mayor and Council”) have a substantial government interest in attempting to preserve the quality of life for the citizens of the Town of Between; and

WHEREAS, the Town of Between, Georgia is authorized by the constitution of the State of Georgia to adopt rules, regulations, laws, and ordinances protecting the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the Town; and

WHEREAS, the Mayor and Council are authorized to regulate the sale and distribution of alcoholic beverages within the town limits pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 36-31-7 and the Charter for the Town of Between; and

WHEREAS, the Mayor and Council have deemed it in the best interest of the health safety and welfare of the citizens of the Town of Between, to adopt an ordinance allowing and regulating the sale of Distilled Spirits in unopened and unbroken packages referred to as “package sales”; and

WHEREAS, O.C.G.A. § 3-4- 41 provides that in the event the governing authority of any municipality desires to exercise the powers authorized by O.C.G.A. § 3-4- 41, which section provides that a municipality may authorize, through proper resolution or ordinance, the issuance of licenses for the package sale of distilled spirits within the Town limits of the Town of Between; and

WHEREAS, 0O.C.G.A. § 3-4- 41(a) authorizes a municipality's governing authority to initiate via resolution or ordinance a voter referendum on the question of whether the issuance of licenses for the package sale of distilled spirits in the political subdivision shall be permitted or prohibited;

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED by the governing authority of the Town of Between, in a regular meeting assembled pursuant to lawful authority thereof, as follows:

SECTION ONE That Chapter _ of the Code of Ordinances of the Town of Between to read as follows:
2:
This ordinance shall be known as the "Packaged Distilled Spirit Ordinance." SEC, 500-102. — Purpose of article.

This article has been enacted in accordance with a plan designed for the following purposes, among others: to promote the health and general welfare of the community, to establish reasonable standards for the regulation and control of the licensing and sales of retail package liquors, to protect and preserve schools and churches, to give effect to existing land use and to preserve certain residential areas, with reasonable considerations, among others, to the character of the areas and their peculiar suitability for particular uses, the congestion in the roads and streets, and with a general view of promoting desirable living conditions and sustaining stability of neighborhood and property values, and to protect against the evils of concentration of the retail outlets for retail package liquor in one (1) family or to prevent undesirable persons from controlling the retail liquor industry.
3: This Chapter shall apply to the licensing and operation of retail package liquor establishments in the Town and, if any section of this chapter conflicts with other provisions in the Town’s code of ordinances, or the general business license requirements of this Code, then this chapter shall control.
4:
- (a) Packaged distilled spirits may be sold in the Town of Between under a license granted by the Mayor and Council upon the terms and conditions provided in this ordinance.

- (b) The business of manufacturing, distributing, selling, handling, and otherwise dealing in or possessing packaged distilled spirits is a privilege and not a right in Georgia. See O.C.G.A. § 3-3-1. All licenses issued pursuant to this ordinance shall be a mere grant of privilege to carry on the business during the term of the license, subject to all terms and conditions imposed by this ordinance and state law. Nothing in this Chapter shall be construed as giving a person a right to sell or otherwise deal in packaged distilled spirits. Distribution and sale of packaged distilled spirits are declared to be privileges in the Town of Between, and not rights.

- (c) All licenses pursuant to this ordinance shall have printed on the front these words: "This license is a mere privilege subject to be revoked and annulled and is subject to any further ordinances that may be enacted."

- (d) Any holder of a license issued in accord with this ordinance is required to apply for and obtain an alcoholic beverage license from the state before any sales commence. Additionally, Town licensees are required to abide by all applicable state regulations and laws.
5: A license is required for the retail sale or wholesale sale of packaged distilled spirits and may be granted by the Mayor and Council upon the terms and conditions as provided in this ordinance.
6:
All definitions set forth in the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code (O.C.G.A. Title 3) and State of Georgia regulations, as amended are hereby adopted by this ordinance. The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this ordinance, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this ordinance, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

Alcohol Treatment Center. Any privately owned, state owned or state operated hospital, community mental health center, or other facility utilized for the diagnosis, care, treatment, or hospitalization of persons who are alcohol dependent and any other hospital or facility within the State of Georgia approved for such purpose by the department.

Applicant means the person, persons, or entity who files forms designated by the Town requesting to be issued a privilege license to sell packaged distilled spirits by either wholesale or retail within the Town.

Application means the forms an applicant is required to file in order apply to obtain a license to sell packaged distilled spirits in the Town.

Bottle means any container, vessel, bottle, or other receptacle used for holding alcoholic beverages. "Unsealed bottle" means any bottle with the original seal cork, cap, or other enclosing device that is either broken, removed, or which the federal revenue strip stamp has been broken.

Church means a permanent building located in an area designated for such use by the zoning ordinances where persons regularly assemble for religious worship, that is publicly designated as a church, but does not include residences or place of businesses also used for religious purposes.

Council means the Town Council of the Town of Between, Georgia.

Distance means the distance established by the most direct route of travel on the ground.

Family member means any person related within the first degree of consanguinity or affinity to the licensee or applicant for a package distilled spirits license.

Federal statutes mean the statutes of the United States now in effect or as may hereinafter be modified.

License means the authorization by the Mayor and Council to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits in the Town.

Licensee means a person, real or artificial, authorized by the Mayor and Council to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits in the Town.

Mayor means the Mayor of the Town of Between, Georgia.

Person means any private individual, partnership, joint venture, corporation, limited liability company or any other business entity or association.

Person underage means an individual under the age of 21 years. Package: A bottle, can, keg, barrel, or other original consumer container.

Packaged distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage with an alcohol volume greater than 24 percent sold or transferred at wholesale or retail in any container, vessel, bottle, or other receptacle used for holding alcoholic beverages.

Packaged distilled spirits retailer means a person licensed by the Mayor and Council to sell packaged distilled spirits in unbroken packages for consumption off premises.

Premises means the property owned, leased, or controlled by the licensee, including but not limited to the building and the parking areas surrounding it, where packaged distilled spirits are sold.

Quality cigars means the sale of handmade cigars rated 85 or above by Cigar Aficionado in the sizes of petite corona, corona, robusto, corona, toro, guordo, panatela, lonsdale, churchill, lancero, double corona and grand corona.

Retail sale means selling or offering for sale packaged distilled spirits to any member of the public.

School means only such state, county, Town, church, or other schools that teach the subjects commonly taught in the common schools and colleges of this state.

State statutes, rules and regulations means all applicable statutes, rules, and regulations of the State of Georgia applicable to the sale of packaged distilled spirits as may now be in effect or which may be amended hereinafter.

Town means the Town of Between, Georgia.

Wholesale means the sale of packaged distilled spirits to any person for the purpose of resale.

Wholesale or wholesale dealer. Any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail dealers, or to retail consumption dealers.

Words importing the masculine gender shall include the feminine and neuter, and the singular shall include the plural.
7: Every person desiring to obtain a license for the retail or wholesale sale of packaged distilled spirits in the Town shall be required under this ordinance to make formal written application to the Mayor and Council for such privilege, which shall be signed by the applicant and/or agent, if applicable, upon forms to be prepared and provided by the Town. All such applicants and agents shall furnish all reasonable data, information and records requested of them by the Town. Failure to furnish such data, information, and records within 30 days from the date of a written request from the Town for such information shall automatically serve to dismiss the application. Applicants, or those having an interest in the application, by filing an application, agree to produce any such data, information, and records for review by the Mayor and Council. Applicants, or those having an interest in the application, by filing an application, agree to submit to an oral interrogation by the Mayor and Council if considered as being important in the ascertainment of the facts relative to an application. The failure to produce such applicant or person of interest within 30 days after being requested in writing to do so shall result in the automatic dismissal of the application. The application must identify the name of the person conducting the business at the premises address contained in the application.
8: Any material omission or untrue or misleading information contained in or left out of an original or renewal application for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits in the Town shall be cause for the denial thereof. If any license has previously been granted based on such misleading statements or material omissions, such shall constitute cause for the revocation of the license.
9: Upon filing an application for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits at wholesale or retail in the Town with the Town Clerk, the Town shall require the applicant to pay a nonrefundable fee to cover the cost of processing the application in the amount of $100.00. Said fee may be amended by resolution of the Mayor and Council as shall be set from time to time. No application shall be processed without payment of fee.
10: The Town shall cause an inquiry to be made into the Town records to determine if an applicant for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits at wholesale or retail in the Town, or other party with an interest in the application, has any outstanding debts or any other monies owing to the Town. No license shall be issued or renewed until such debts are paid in full.
11: Upon an application for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits at wholesale or retail in the Town being granted by the Mayor and Council, a license shall be issued to the applicant as of the date the applicant commences his/her alcoholic beverage business and upon the payment by the applicant of the license fee.
12: The dental of an application for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits at wholesale or retail in the Town shall be in writing, with the reasons therefore stated, and it shall be mailed or delivered to the applicant at the address of the applicant contained on the application by first class mail. Any applicant aggrieved by the decision of the Mayor and Council regarding the denial of a license shall be afforded a hearing with an opportunity to present evidence and cross examine opposing witnesses as provided herein.
13: When any application for a retail or wholesale package distilled spirits license is denied for cause, or any license is revoked for cause by the Mayor and Council, the Town Clerk shall not accept or consider any application by such applicant for a license to operate the same type of business for a period of 24 months from the date of a license denial and 60 months from the date of a revocation of license in the event of a revocation for cause.
14:
An application for a proposed retail package distilled spirits license may be approved by the Mayor and Council prior to the applicant obtaining an occupancy permit for a premise if the premises is currently, or will be, under construction. If approved by the Mayor and Council, the Town shall not issue the license until the applicant has obtained an occupancy permit and all other approvals required by the state and Town for building code purposes, and the applicant has advised the Town in writing of the date on which the business shall commence, which date shall not exceed 12 months from the date of application approval. The license shall be dated as of such commencement date and shall not be effective until that date. If the applicant fails to obtain an occupancy permit within 12 months of the date of approval of the application to sell packaged distilled spirits at retail in the Town, the applicant shall forfeit his application which shall, by

virtue of failure to obtain an occupancy permit, be rejected without the necessity of any further action of the Mayor and Council.
15: Except for a license issued to a site under construction, or soon to be under construction, an applicant must open the retail package distilled spirits business in the establishment referred to in the application within six months after its approval by Mayor and Council. The Town Clerk shall not issue the license until presented with the applicant's notarized statement stating the applicant is in fact the owner of the business and will open for business on a date certain. The license shall be dated as of the date certain in the affidavit and shall not be effective until that date. Failure to open the licensed establishment within the six-month period or the date stated in the applicant's affidavit shall serve an automatic forfeiture and cancellation of the unused license, and no refund of fees shall be made.
16: Any holder of a license issued under this ordinance, who shall begin the operation of the business authorized in the license, but who shall for a period of six consecutive months thereafter cease to operate the business as authorized in the license, shall, upon completion of the sixmonth period, automatically forfeit his license. Said license shall, by virtue of the failure to operate, be revoked without the necessity of any further action of the Mayor and Council.
17: No person who has any direct financial interest in a license for the sale of package distilled spirits at wholesale shall hold any other license or an interest in any license under the terms of this ordinance.
18: It shall be lawful for a licensee to sell packaged distilled spirits at retail at a designated premises location in the Town provided that such sales are made in strict compliance with all federal statutes, all state laws, rules and regulations, and all provisions of this ordinance, and provided that such licensee has a valid and duly issued privilege license from the Town permitting him or her to sell same. Transfer of ownership or possession of any retail or wholesale packaged distilled spirits license is prohibited, void and invalid.
19: Each licensee shall be responsible for all acts of such licensee as well as the acts of the licensee's officers, employees, agents, and representatives. Any violation of this ordinance by any officer, employee, agent, or representative of a licensee shall constitute a violation of this ordinance by such licensee.
20:
Citizenship, age, and residency requirements for an applicant for a license to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be as follows:

- (1) Ifthe applicant is a person, the person shall be a United States citizen, or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residency, a resident of the Town, and at least 21 years of age; provided, however, the person applicant need not be a Town resident if the person designates a resident of the Town who is at least 21 years of age as his or her agent who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license.

- (2) If the applicant is a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or other legal entity, this section shall apply to all its partners, officers, managers, and principal owners. If a corporation or limited liability company, the license shall be issued to the corporation or limited liability company. Where the principal owner or member is not a resident of the Town, the corporation or limited liability company shall designate an individual as its agent who must be a resident of the Town and at least 21 years of age who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license. For a partnership, the license shall be issued to one of the partners. If a partner is not a resident of the Town, the partnership must designate a Town resident at least 21 years of age as the partnership's agent who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license.

- (3) Any change in any relationship declared in this ordinance must be filed, when said change is made, with the mayor, or his designee, and failure to do so within a period of 30 days after such change is made shall be grounds for revocation of a license granted under this ordinance by the Mayor and Council.
21:
No application for any license required under this ordinance shall be granted where the application, investigation or the evidence presented at a hearing before the Mayor and Council shows any of the following conditions to exist:

- (1) The applicant, principal owner, or his agent has a conviction, as defined in subparagraph (5) of this section or does not have sufficient mental capaTown to conduct the business for which application is made or who has been dishonorably discharged from the armed services of the United States.

- (2) The applicant or any agent, stockholder, partner, or member of the applicant has had any license issued by the Town previously revoked within 36 months of the date of the application.

- (3) The applicant or his agent, as a previous holder of a license to sell any type of alcoholic beverages in any jurisdiction, has violated any law, regulation or ordinance relating to such business within a 36-month period immediately preceding the date of the application. In

the event of a renewal application, offences prosecuted and resolved pursuant to this ordinance shall not be considered.

- (4) The applicant's proposed business premise is not properly zoned for the license applied for.

- (5) Persons with prior felony criminal convictions.

- a. The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

- 1. "Convictions" include an adjudication of guilt, a plea of guilty, a plea of nolo contendere, a guilty plea under a first offender statute, or the forfeiture of a bond when charged with a felony;

- 2. "Principal owner" refers to an individual owning, directly or indirectly, a five percent or more interest in a corporation, partnership, limited partnership, limited liability company or other entity.

- b. No license for the sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be issued to any individual, partnership, limited partnership, corporation or limited liability company where such individual or any individual who is a principal owner of any partnership, limited partnership, corporation, limited liability company or other entity, or who is the agent responsible for matters relating to the license shall have been convicted under any federal, state or local law of any misdemeanor involving sexual misconduct, dishonesty, possession or use of a controlled substance, or possession of drug paraphernalia within ten years prior to the filing of the application for such license; or, convicted under any federal state or local law of any felony within ten years prior to the filing of the application for such license.
22:
- (a) No license for the sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be transferable, except as otherwise provided in this section.

- (b) If an individual licensee dies, the licensee's estate shall be allowed to continue to sell packaged distilled spirits for a period of 60 days from the date of death, or until expiration of the license, or until approval of a new licensee, whichever shall first occur. However, no sale of alcoholic beverages shall be allowed until such time as a personal representative of the estate, appointed by a probate court of competent jurisdiction, shall make application with the Town Clerk for authorization to continue to sell for such period.

- (c) If a licensee or responsible person, other than the owner, severs such licensees association with a licensed establishment, the establishment may continue to sell packaged distilled spirits for a period of 60 days from the date of such severance, provided a new application is filed with the Town Clerk within ten days of such severance, and indicates that

there has been no change in the ownership of the licensed establishment. If approved by the Mayor and Council, the term of the new license shall be for the remaining term of the original license and the original license shall terminate as of the date of such approval. No additional license fees, other than administrative fee set by the Mayor and Council by resolution from time to time, shall be required from the applicant.

- (d) Nothing in this section, however, shall prohibit one or more of the partners in a partnership holding a license to withdraw from the partnership in favor of one or more of the partners who were partners at the time of the issuance of the license and who meet the qualifications of a licensee under this article. This subsection shall not prohibit the transfer of stock between persons who held stock in the corporation at the time of issuance of the license, nor shall it prohibit transfers of stock which do not result in any person increasing such person's holdings by a total of ten percent or more of any class stock.

- (e) Except as provided in this section, any change in the ownership of any entity granted a license shall cancel and revoke any license issued automatically, without the necessity of any hearing.
23:
- (a) Any licensee authorized to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits at specifically described premises shall be required to surrender the license held without demand, except as otherwise provided in this ordinance, upon any of the following events: Any sale or transfer of an interest in the business of the licensee, whether by an actual sale of any of the licensee's stock or proprietorship or partnership interest to any unregistered person not identified in the licensee's application or upon a sale of all or substantially all of the licensee's assets to any unregistered person. For purposes of this subsection, the term "unregistered person" shall mean any individual, corporation, partnership, limited partnership, club, or association, not shown upon any current application for the specific premises involved. For purposes of this subsection, a sale of all or substantially all the licensee's assets shall include or be deemed to include any bulk sale of inventory or assets at any specifically described premises for which the license holder is licensed to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits in the Town. For purposes of this subsection, any corporation or limited partnership or association whose stock is traded on any stock exchange recognized by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission shall be excepted from this requirement to the extent of any transfer of shareholding or partnership interests not exceeding five percent in any one trade or transaction.

- (b) Time limit. Surrender as provided in this chapter shall be made to the Town Clerk within 30 days of any event requiring surrender of the license.

- (c) Fines for failure to surrender. For failure to surrender the license within the period provided in subsection (b) of this section, the applicant shall be fined an amount as follows:

- (1) The sum of $50.00 for failure to surrender within 30 days of the date that any surrender of the alcoholic beverage license is required: and

- (2) An additional sum of $10.00 per day for each day thereafter from which the licensee fails or defaults in the surrender of the license after the date upon which the surrender is required.

- (d) The Town Clerk shall assess any penalty against any licensee for failure to surrender the license as required by this section. Notice of assessment shall be by certified letter to the licensee based upon information and belief of the Town Clerk stating the date that any required surrender should have been made by the licensee. The licensee shall have a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the certified letter from the Town Clerk of the notice of assessment of the penalty to protest the assessment to the Town Clerk by presenting evidence or information in writing to the Town Clerk as to the licensee's position. If the Town Clerk shall not agree with the licensee's position, the licensee shall have ten days from the date of the written notice of the Town Clerk's written decision disagreeing with the licensee's protest to request in writing a hearing before the Mayor and Council. The Town Clerk shall forward the protest to the Mayor and Council who shall at its next regular meeting accept, reject, or modify the assessment of the penalty.
24:
A license issued under this article shall expire automatically and without notice upon the occurrence of a delinquency of 20 days in:

- (1) Filing any required monthly report under this chapter; or

- (2) Paying over any required excise tax levied under this chapter or any other indebtedness owed to the Town.

Sec, 500-125. - Revocation of state license.

Whenever the Georgia Department of Revenue shall revoke any permit or license to sell at wholesale or retail any packaged distilled spirits, any license issued under this ordinance for the same licensed premises shall thereupon be automatically revoked without any action by the Mayor and Council, or any Town officer, and the licensee shall not be entitled to any refund of any license fee theretofore paid to the Town.
25: The Mayor is delegated the authority to suspend any license issued under this ordinance for due cause in any emergency situation, and the suspension shall be made effective immediately and shall remain in force until a hearing before the Mayor and Council is held pursuant to Section 500-128, Section 500-129, and Section 500-130.
26: When the Mayor finds a violation of any section of this ordinance for which the licensee shall have his packaged distilled spirits license suspended or revoked, all alcoholic beverage licenses of the licensee under this article shall be so suspended or revoked.
27:
- (a) Due cause hearing; defined; cost of hearing.

- (1) No license which has been issued or which may be issued pursuant to this article shall be suspended or revoked, except as provided in Sec. _-125, except for due cause and after a hearing as provided in this ordinance.

- (b) The term "due cause" for the purposes of this chapter of the Code shall include, but not be limited to:

- (1) Conviction of, or the entering of a plea of guilty, plea of first offender, or plea of nolo contendere by the licensee or any person holding an interest in the license for any felony, any law, administrative regulation, or ordinance involving alcoholic beverages, gambling or narcotics, or tax laws.

- (2) Conviction of, or the entering of a plea of guilty, plea of first offender, or plea of nolo contendere by the licensee or any person holding an interest in the license for any sex offense, or when the licensee permits on-premises consumption.

- (3) Material falsification of any fact given in an application for a license issued under this ordinance or bearing upon the licensee's qualification therefore. Any act, which may be construed as a subterfuge to circumvent any of the qualifications for a license under this ordinance.

- (4) Violation of any provision of this ordinance, or any failure to meet or maintain any standard or regulation prescribed by this ordinance as a condition or qualification for holding a license.

- (5) Any other factor known to or discovered by the Town whereby it is objectively shown the licensee, any of the licensee's employees or any person holding an interest in a license, has engaged in conduct at or involving the licensed business or has permitted conduct on the licensed premises that constitutes a violation of federal or state law, local ordinance or administrative regulations involving alcoholic beverages, gambling, narcotics or sex offenses. Same shall create a rebuttable presumption that the violative act was done with the knowledge or consent of the licensee.
28: The Town Clerk shall notify the licensee of any charge of conduct or offense subject to penalty, suspension or revocation or any combination thereof. If the potential sanction is suspension or revocation the notice shall also state, the place and time the Mayor and Council will hear the charges against the licensee. The notice may also contain additional information as the Town Clerk may deem appropriate. The notice shall be delivered to the licensee at least five days prior to the hearing date, by personal delivery, or by first class mail addressed to the licensee at the address contained in licensee's application, or by posting the notice on the front door of the licensed premises. In the case of delivery by first class mail the notice shall be deemed delivered two days after being deposited into the U.S. mail properly addressed and with adequate postage.
29: The Mayor and Council shall conduct a hearing on the record on any revocation or suspension of a packaged distilled spirits license. The licensee shall be allowed to appear at said hearing and to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses. The Mayor and Council shall notify the licensee of its decision as to revocation or suspension of the license at such hearing or in writing no later than 30 days after such hearing. Upon a finding by the Mayor and Council that sufficient evidence exists to support the revocation or suspension, the Mayor and Council may revoke or suspend the license of the licensee for up to a period not to exceed 60 months. Failure of the Mayor and Council to notify the licensee of its determination at such hearing or in writing no later than 30 days after such hearing shall result in a dismissal of the charge.
30: When an alcoholic beverage license is revoked, suspended or expires, the Town shall not be required to refund any portion of the license fee.
31: When any license for selling packaged distilled spirits is revoked, suspended, or automatically expires, all signs indicating that such packaged distilled spirits may be sold or purchased at that premises shall be removed from the premises, both outside and inside.
32:
- (1) The number of packaged distilled spirits licenses for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits in the Town, issued under this ordinance and outstanding within the Town of Between, shall be limited to a total of two licenses.

- (2) With respect to the issuance of the first two retail sale of distilled spirits licenses, if more than one properly completed application is submitted to the Town for and approved by the Mayor and Council at the time of the publicly announced deadline for applications

has expired, the Town will then have a lottery drawing where more than one properly completed application is approved by the Mayor and Council. In the event the Town does not receive an application by the deadline mentioned above, the Town will then accept additional properly completed applications for an additional 30 days with a lottery to follow if there are more than one properly completed applications approved by the Mayor and Council. If no applications are received during the second period, the license will then be awarded to the first qualified applicant. In the event of a surrender, suspension for more than 180 days, or the revocation of a retail distilled spirits license, the Town will hold a lottery drawing for the vacant license with such lottery being held not less than 60 days from the effective date of such suspension, surrender, termination, or revocation. With respect to such lottery, the Town shall issue public notice for the submission of applications not less than 30 days prior to the date of the lottery drawing. For purposes of this section, the effective date shall be the date upon which all appeals, if any, are no longer available to a licensee or have otherwise been exhausted.

- (4) If an applicant that is selected by lottery fails to complete the process required by the Town to obtain a license to sell packaged distilled spirits within the time limits set forth in this ordinance, then the Town will select by lottery another applicant from the previous pool of properly submitted applications.
33:
- (a) No retail or wholesale packaged distilled spirits license shall be issued until it has been approved by the Mayor and Council.

- (b) No retail or wholesale packaged distilled spirits license shall be approved unless all sections of this ordinance, state laws, rules and regulations have been met by the applicant.
34: Every license issued under this article shall be a mere grant or privilege to carry on such business during the term of the license, subject to all the terms and conditions imposed by ordinance and related laws, applicable sections of state law, rules and regulations and other Town ordinances and resolutions relating to such business.
35: A packaged distilled spirits licensee may hold more than one type of retail license, including but not limited to wine and malt beverage, provided that each license must be approved by the Mayor and Council. Licensees seeking more than one licenses for an individual premise must meet the requirements of each license, including the payment for each separate license as more fully set out in other chapters of the Town’s code of ordinances.
36:
It shall be unlawful for a licensee to engage in any activity pertaining to the sale of alcoholic beverages except as authorized by the type of license held.

Sec, 500-138. - Limitations on use.

- (a) It shall be unlawful for any person operating a premise licensed for the retail sale of wine and malt beverages to store or have on the premises any packaged distilled spirits for retail sales without a license therefore.

- (b) Packaged distilled spirits licensees shall not be permitted to sell packaged distilled spirits for home delivery.

- (c) Packaged distilled spirits licensees shall not be permitted to sell packaged distilled spirits through a drive through window, door, or other convenience.

- (d) Packaged distilled spirits licensees shall not be permitted to operate, store, or maintain power coin operated amusement machines in the business premises licensed to sell by retail packaged distilled spirits. No form of entertainment, including pinball machines, lottery, bingo, music machines or similar devices, shall be permitted in any premises used for packaged retail distilled spirits sales. No seating facilities, other than for employees, shall be permitted.
37: Each licensee for the sale of packaged distilled spirits shall have his license posted conspicuously in the place of business. The failure of a licensee to display the license conspicuously in his place of business shall be a violation of this ordinance.
38:
- (a) A license issued for the retail package sales of distilled spirits shall be valid only for the operation of said purpose upon the property proposed in the licensee's application and any change of location shall be cause for revocation of the license.

- (b) No retail package distilled spirits license shall be issued for the operation of same where such would be a prohibited use under the Town's zoning ordinance in effect at time of issuance.

- (c) No license for the sale of packaged distilled spirits at retail shall be issued for a location where the proposed place of business is located on property the owner of which has any direct or indirect interest or association, including ownership, financial or governing, in any other property within the Town of Between that operates another retail or wholesale packaged distilled spirits business. For purposes of this section, "owner" shall mean and include an individual, partner, corporation, company, association, or other business entity.

- (d) To assure that these requirements are satisfied, no original or renewal license shall be issued for any location until a majority of the members of the Council have approved the proposed location as being suitable for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits after a consideration of this matter at a properly advertised public meeting of the Council.
39: No license to engage in the package sale of spirituous liquors shall be issued within the areas described in this article unless the location has been zoned B-2, General Business or P-B- D, Planned Business Development.
40:
- (a) The physical locations designated by an applicant for use in the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be a newly constructed free-standing building. The front and both sides of the building must have a brick, stone, or stucco facade. The remaining exterior elevations must meet applicable Town of Between building requirements. Retail packaged distilled spirits premises shall not be made from or out of a manufactured, movable or any prefabricated type of building.

- (b) The minimum square footage of the premises display area within a structure shall be 5,000 square feet. The maximum square footage of the premises display area within a structure shall be 15,000 square feet. Excess storage, not including display areas, must be no less than 500 square feet within the structure but separate from the retail display floor. No separate modules or buildings are allowed, and no storage is permitted outside. The rear of the structure shall be painted a neutral color to blend with the surrounding area.

- (c) All premises in the Town used for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be located on a ground floor level. Each premises shall have only one main entrance for use by the public as a means of ingress and egress for the purpose of purchasing packaged distilled spirits at retail. Notwithstanding, when a premise is located on the corner of two public streets such premises may maintain a door opening on each of the public streets.

- (d) All premises used by a licensee for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits shall have night lights surrounding the premises and shall be equipped with a functioning security system, which includes a burglar alarm system on the inside of the premises and at least one indoor and one outdoor camera with video storage capability. Security bars or other types of window or door obstructions are prohibited.

- (e) The windows in such premises of licensee shall not be obstructed or obscured by any object, including, but not limited to signage, shelves, inventory, or displays and shall be arranged so that passersby and law enforcement personnel on the street can view the premises by looking through windows opening onto the streets. This requirement shall apply to all sides of structures facing streets. Proposed plans and drawings must be furnished to the Mayor and Council as a part of the application. All plans for such premises must receive approval from the Mayor and Council prior to the commencement of construction.

- (f) All premises utilized by a licensee for the purpose of retail packaged distilled spirits sales shall be subject to applicable zoning, building, and Town land development regulations.

- (g) A license issued under this ordinance for a retail package distilled spirits sales location shall be valid only for the operation of such business upon the property proposed in the application and any change of location shall be cause for revocation of the license.

- (h) No license shall be issued for the operation of a retail packaged distilled spirits ren effect at time of issuance.
41: Sworn officers of the Walton County Sheriff's Office, Town officials and representatives, and/or Walton County code enforcement officers shall have the authority to inspect establishments licensed under this ordinance during the hours in which the premises are open for business. These inspections shall be made for the purpose of verifying compliance with the requirements of this ordinance and state law. This section is not intended to limit the authority of any other Town officer to conduct inspections authorized by other sections of the Town of Between Code of Ordinances or state law.
42: An annual retail and wholesale packaged distilled spirits license fee shall be paid in advance on or before January 15th of each year, in the sum of $5,000.00 by certified check, or in such other form of payment as authorized by the Mayor and Council. Any new license granted during a calendar year shall not be prorated for the remainder of the calendar year. In addition to the annual packaged distilled spirits license, the licensee will be required to pay and maintain a business license for the sum of $100.00 annually.
43:
- (a) A distilled spirit tasting permit for purposes of this section shall be limited to a person possessing a current license from the Town for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits and a valid current distilled spirits license from the state.

- (b) Any tasting occurring on the premises of a business possessing a tasting permit shall be limited to an area that is separated from the retail area of the premises by walls or other partitions that prohibit pedestrian traffic through the tasting area.

- (c) An eligible licensee may petition the Town for a tasting permit provided the licensee holds a valid license for the sale of packaged distilled spirits issued by the Town.

- (d) A tasting permit shall allow the licensee to offer or sell samples in connection with an instructional or educational promotion and the samples must be consumed in the presence of a representative of the licensed business.

- (e) A tasting permit shall allow the permittee to offer 26 tasting events per year, for no more than one time per day, for a maximum of four hours, and only during the hours the licensed premises may lawfully sell unbroken packages of distilled spirits.

- (f) A tasting event may only include one type of distilled spirit per event, may include more than one brand of each type of distilled spirit, and no more than four brands may be open at any one time during the tasting event.

- (g) A tasting permit shall be subject to all laws, rules and regulations of the Town and state, including O.C.G.A. § 3-3-26 and Rule 560-2-5-05 of the state department of revenue, alcohol, and tobacco division, and shall be subject to suspension or revocation for violation thereof.

- (h) Said tasting permit need only be applied for once and may be automatically renewed when said packaged distilled spirits license is renewed. Provided, however, that the Town may revoke or suspend such tasting permit and/or impose such conditions on its operation at the Town's discretion for violation of this ordinance or in furtherance of the health, safety, and welfare of the Town's inhabitants.
44: All wholesalers licensed under this ordinance shall file a certified statement with the Town of their gross sales in the Town for the preceding calendar month on or before the 20th of the following month.
45: Distilled spirits deliveries and sales by wholesalers under this ordinance shall only be made to retailers that are properly licensed for the operation of retail packaged distilled spirits sales in the Town. Deliveries shall be made in a conveyance owned and operated by the licensed wholesaler, Deliveries of inventory shall only occur at the rear of the premises through the designated rear entrance to the premises.
46:
Retail licensees under this ordinance shall not buy or accept deliveries of packaged distilled spirits from wholesalers not licensed under this ordinance. Retail licensees under this ordinance shall only accept deliveries of packaged distilled spirits to the premises for which the license is issued and by no means other than a conveyance owned and operated by a wholesaler licensed as required by this ordinance. However, by written request to the Mayor and Council and upon the granting of permission by the Mayor and Council in writing, deliveries may, in

special instances, be made otherwise upon the terms and conditions as prescribed by the Mayor and Council as to each such delivery.
47: It shall be a violation of this ordinance for any person to sell at retail within the Town any distilled spirits on which the taxes provided for in this ordinance have not been paid.
48: In addition to all other taxes or license fees imposed upon retail dealers engaged in the Town in the business of selling distilled spirits, as defined in this chapter, there is imposed and levied upon all such licensees an excise tax, to be computed and collected as set forth in this ordinance.
49:
Each wholesale dealer or distributor selling, shipping, or delivering distilled spirits to any retail packaged distilled spirits licensee in the Town shall, as a condition of the privilege of carrying on such business in the Town:

- (1) Keep true and correct records of all sales, shipments, or deliveries of such distilled spirits to each retail licensee in the Town. Such records shall be preserved for a period of two years and shall be made available on request for the inspection of any duly authorized Town representative.

- (2) Collect from each such retail licensee in the Town, at the time of delivery of the distilled spirits, the amount of tax due under this ordinance and hold the money in trust for the Town until such amount is remitted to the Town as provided in subsection (3) of this section.

- (3) On or before the 20th day of each calendar month, make a verified and comprehensive report to the Town which shall correctly show all sales and deliveries of distilled spirits to or for each retail licensee in the Town for the month immediately preceding the report. The report shall show the name and address of each retail licensee, quantities delivered to each retail licensee, the amount of tax collected under the terms of this ordinance and such other information as may be called for by the Town. The report shall be accompanied by remittance to the Town for all taxes collected or due as shown on the report. There is assessed a ten percent late charge on the gross tax due for the month. Delinquent amounts shall bear interest at an annual rate equal to the bank prime loan rate as posted by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System in statistical release H. 15 or any publication that may supersede it, plus three percent, to accrue monthly. Such annual interest rate shall be determined for each calendar year based on the first weekly posting of statistical release of H. 15 on or after January 1st of each calendar year.
50: It shall be unlawful and a violation of this division for any person to deliver any distilled spirits to any retail licensee in the Town without collecting the taxes provided for in this division at the time of delivery,
51: If any wholesale dealer or distributor fails or refuses to make the reports provided for in this division, the Town shall notify the licensee in writing. If the reports are not made and the taxes remitted within five days from the date of the notice, the Town may withdraw from the wholesale dealer or distributor the privilege of doing business in the Town by revoking the license.
52: The tax imposed in this division shall be computable and payable monthly.
53: In addition to the license fees established by this Chapter, there is hereby levied and imposed a specific excise tax on the sale of packaged distilled spirits within the Town, in the amount of $0.22 per liter of distilled spirits, excluding fortified wine, and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of a liter. The excise tax as provided for in this section shall be imposed upon and shall be paid by the licensed wholesale dealer in distilled spirits by the package. The requirements for paying and filing of returns by such wholesale dealer shall be as provided in
55: The filing of a false or fraudulent report under this division shall render the wholesale dealer making such report liable for a penalty equal to ten percent of the amount of the remittance which would be required under an accurate and truthful report. In addition to other penalties provided in this division, the failure to make a timely report or remittance or the filing of a false or fraudulent report under this division shall also constitute grounds for the revocation of the business license issued by the Town to a wholesale dealer.

erroneously or illegally collected.

At any time within three years after any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected pursuant to this division becomes due and payable, and at any time within three years after the delinquency of any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected, the Mayor and Council may bring an action in the courts of this state, any other state, or of the United States in the name

of the Town to collect the amount delinquent, together with penalties and interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees, and other legal fees incident thereto. Whenever the amount of any tax, penalty or interest has been paid more than once or has been paid erroneously or illegally collected or received by the Town under this division, it may be offset against any future liability for the tax. If the licensee determines that he has overpaid or paid more than once, which fact has not been determined by the Town, he will have three years from the date of payment to file a claim in writing stating the specific ground upon which the claim is founded. The claim shall be audited. If the claim is approved by the Mayor and Council, the excess amount paid the Town may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the person by whom it was paid or from his administrators or executors.
57: Unless state laws and regulations hereafter provide otherwise, packaged distilled spirits may be sold at retail only between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 11:30 p.m., Monday through Saturday, including on Election Day. Packaged distilled spirits may be sold at retail on Sundays and holidays from 12:30 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. The hours of operation of wholesale licensees for the distribution of beer and wine within the Town shall be between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
58: It shall be unlawful for any person issued a license under this division to make deliveries of any distilled spirits by the package beyond the boundaries of the premises covered by the license.
59: It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or dispense distilled spirits from drive-in or service windows. Violation of this section will result in suspension or revocation for cause of the license.
60: No retail license for the package sales of distilled spirits shall be allowed in or in connection with the operation of any restaurant, cafe or eating place, or in the same room where a bar is maintained for the dispensing and sale of malt beverages, wine by the drink, or distilled spirits by the drink, or any other business establishment, except as may be permitted herein by this division. Nothing in this section, however, shall be construed to limit or prohibit distilled spirit tasting events.
61: Under this division it shall be unlawful for licensees or their agents to add to the contents of a bottle or to refill empty bottles or in any other manner to misrepresent the quantity, quality, or brand name of any alcoholic beverage.
62: No person issued a license under this chapter or any other person on the licensed premises shall sell any alcoholic beverages to any person in an intoxicated condition.
63:
There must be present on the premises an inventory of retail goods and merchandise available for sale having a retail value of not less than $500,000.00, at all times.

- (a) For purposes of measuring whether a licensee's inventory of retail goods and merchandise has a value of at least $500,000.00, there must be an average monthly inventory based upon the inventory records for the specific premises of at least $500,000.00.

- (b) Each license holder at the premises shall have his monthly inventory records showing the retail value of all goods and merchandise on the premises at the location of the premises at all times during regular business hours for inspection by the Walton County Sheriff, his designee or codes enforcement.

- (c) No licensee licensed to sell packaged distilled spirits shall sell, offer for sale, display, or keep in stock for sale or furnish at its licensed location where distilled spirits are offered for sale, any other products, or services, except the following:

- (1) Wines, if the licensee holds a valid and current license to sell wine at that premises;

- (2) Malt beverages, if the licensee holds a valid and current license to sell malt beverages at that premises;

- (3) Paper, styrofoam, plastic cups, gift bags, which are limited in size to accommodate one 750 ml size bottle of wine or spirits.

- (4) Bar supplies, corkscrews, openers, straws, swizzle stirrers, and bar-related containers, and wares made of glass, plastic, metal or ceramic materials, cocktail olives, onions, cherries, lemons, limes, and sugars or salts produced and marketed specifically for tie preparation of alcoholic beverage drinks, alcoholic beverage drink recipe booklets, bar guides and consumer-oriented alcoholic beverage publications.

- (5) Quality cigars.
64: It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly and intentionally sell any alcoholic beverage for consumption on premises where packaged distilled spirits are sold, except in connection with a tasting permit.
65: Proper identification as used in this division shall mean any document issued by a governmental agency containing a description of the person, such person's photograph, or both, and such person's date of birth. Proper identification includes, without being limited to, a passport, military identification card, driver's license, or the identification card authorized under O.C.G.A. § 40-5-100 through 40-5-104. Proper identification shall not include a birth certificate and shall not include any traffic citation and complaint form.
66: It shall be the responsibility of the licensee to examine the proper identification of each patron desiring to purchase packaged distilled spirits to ascertain that such patron is 21 years of age or older. Packaged distilled spirits shall not be sold to anyone younger than 21 years of age.
67:
- (a) Fora retail packaged distilled spirits license to be issued, the premises of the applicant must meet the following distance requirements:

- (1) The premises shall not be located in or within 100 yards of an alcoholic treatment center owned and operated privately or by the state, the county, or the Town.

- (2) The premises shall not be located in or within 100 yards of any church building, housing authority property, or within 200 yards of any school building, educational building, or school grounds.

- (3) No new retail package liquor licensed place of business or the relocation of an existing retail package liquor licensed place of business engaged in the retail package sale of distilled spirits shall be located within 1,760 yards (1 mile) of any other business licensed to engage in the retail sale of distilled spirits as measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.

- (4) The most direct route of pedestrian travel on the ground shall be along the right-ofway measured from the nearest building wall of any church or nearest property line of any school, public housing, or public recreation area to the center of any door of customer entry of the proposed premises of the applicant.
68:
additional information.

- (a) All applications for licenses under this article, both original and renewal, must be accompanied by a full and complete statement under oath of information describing any and all interests, as defined by state law, in the person licensed or to be licensed. This information shall include the names and addresses of any person who has any ownership interest in the person licensed or to be licensed and the size of such interest; the specific street address of any other premises which is authorized for retail sale of alcoholic beverages by the package in which the person licensed or to be licensed has any ownership interest; detailed description of the ownership or leasehold of premises where the person licensed or to be licensed is or will be operating, including but not limited to an executed copy of the vesting deed or lease; and the name and address of any owner and lessor of the premises in which the person licensed or to be licensed is or will be operating.

- (b) Any change in the information required in subsection (a) must be filed with the Town Clerk when the change occurs, and failure to do so within a period of ten days of such change shall be grounds for denial, probation, suspension or revocation, as may apply, by the Council.
69:
- (a) No packaged distilled spirits shall be sold at retail except in Retail businesses or premises in which space has been set aside and devoted substantially to the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits, with ingress and egress provided directly to, and only to, the exterior of the buildings in which the business or premises is located and not any other enclosed part of the building in which such business or premises is located, except as provided hereafter.

- (b) Each licensee for the retail sale of distilled spirits by the package shall have conspicuously displayed within the interior of their business or premises not less than four copies of a printed price list of the distilled spirits offered for sale, provided that a licensee, in lieu of having four copies of a printed price list, may have the prices placed on the bottles or on the front of the shelf where distilled spirits are exhibited for sale.

- (c) No exterior signs may be used to advertise the price of any distilled spirits offered for sale at the business or premises of a person licensed for retail sale of distilled spirits by the package.

- (d) No price or prices for the retail sale of distilled spirits shall be displayed in any show window or any place visible from the outside the premises where retail packaged distilled spirits are sold.
70:
No person with a license for the retail sale of distilled spirits by the package shall permit on their premises any coin operated amusement machine, including but not limited to a slot machine, mechanical music box or pinball machine, or any form of electronic or mechanical game

machine or coin-operated device, which might be used for entertainment or amusement purposes, except pursuant to applicable state law.
71: The license for the retail sale of distilled spirits by the package shall be displayed on a front window or entrance of the licensed premises, with the name of the licensee, together with the inscription "Town of Between License for Retail Sale of Distilled Spirits by the Package, No. __," and the letters, numbers and symbols on the license shall be not less than four inches, nor more than eight inches, in height. The license shall at all times be kept in plain view within the licensed premises or business.
72:
delivery to licensed retail dealer; marking of vehicles.

- (a) No person who has any financial interest in a wholesale dealer license for the sale of distilled spirits shall be issued any license for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits.

- (b) No distilled spirits shall be delivered to any licensed retail dealer in the Town except by a licensed wholesale dealer, who shall make such deliveries by a vehicle owned by the wholesaler, with the wholesaler's name clearly marked on the outside of the vehicle.
73:
Upon adoption of this Ordinance, a certified copy of the same shall be forwarded to the Walton County Election Superintendent, who shall include the following question on the May 21, 2024 election ballot:

"()YES Shall the issuance of licenses for the package sale of distilled ()NO _ spirits be approved?"

Those desiring to vote in favor of the issuance of the licenses shall vote "Yes." Those desiring to vote against the issuance of the licenses shall vote "No."
74:
- (a) In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 3-4:41(a) and (b), upon receipt and validation of this Ordinance, the Walton County Election Superintendent shall call and conduct a referendum election as provided for in Chapter 2 of Title 21, the "Georgia Election Code", and on a date authorized under O.C.G.A. § 21:2:540.

- (b) The Walton County Election Superintendent is hereby authorized and directed to place an advertisement in the Walton Tribune newspaper once a week for (2) two weeks immediately prior to the date of the May 21, 2024, election where the above questions shall be placed on the ballot, stating in the advertisement (1) the date and purpose of the referendum to be placed on the ballot; and (2) the full text of the question to be placed on the ballot.
75:
Section One of this Ordinance shall become effective upon June 4, 2024, so long as the referendum authorized by this Ordinance is approved by the majority of votes cast on the question to be placed on the May 21, 2024, election ballot, and the Election Superintendent certifies that result. If the referendum is not approved by a majority of the votes cast, Section One of this Ordinance shall be null and void.

SEVERABILITY. If any section, provision or clause of any part of this ordinance shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional, or if the provisions of any part of this ordinance as applied to any particular situation or set of circumstances shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional, such invalidity shall not be construed to affect the portions of this ordinance not so held to be invalid, or the application of this ordinance to other circumstances not so held to be invalid. It is hereby declared as the intent that this ordinance would have been adopted had such invalid portion not been included herein.

REPEALER PROVISION. Any and all existing or pre-existing Town of Between ordinances, amendments and/or resolutions or parts of ordinances or resolutions in conflict herewith are repealed.
